channel.title: The Grant Desk - AI, Tech & Research, UK, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: AI, Tech & Research, UK, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Grant: University of Exeter Arts and Culture: Arts Commission 2026/27 (organisational cultures and narrative infrastructure) (closes 29 Nov)
item.description:
University of Exeter Arts and Culture, with the Faculty of Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences (HASS)
Deadline: 29 Nov 2026
Award: Artist fee GBP 14,000 (incl. VAT, also covering travel, subsistence and accommodation) plus a production and presentation budget of up to GBP 4,000; a freelance creative producer is paid separately. Interviewed candidates receive GBP 100. No application fee.

The University of Exeter's annual flagship Arts Commission invites a creative practitioner in any artform interested in organisational cultures (how people work together in formal settings, and how those cultures can be disrupted, adjusted and reimagined) to work with academics in the Faculty of...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: Screen South Showcase Artists 2026-27, Round 2 (digital creative bursaries up to GBP 1,500) (closes 29 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Screen South
Deadline: 29 Jan 2027
Award: Bursaries up to GBP 1,500 plus possible exhibition space.

Screen South supports digital creative projects (visual, immersive and sound-based) that are already underway and can be shown within six months; linear film is unlikely to be funded. ELIGIBILITY: artists based in South East England, excluding London.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: Awesome Foundation Local Chapters: USD 1,000 Monthly Micro-grants (US, UK, Canada, Australia, NL, Asia) (rolling)
item.description:
Awesome Foundation (local chapters)
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Usually USD 1,000 (or local equivalent) per grant, no strings attached, typically one grant per chapter per month. No application fee.

The Awesome Foundation is a network of volunteer giving circles: in each chapter about ten trustees pool their own money to give a USD 1,000 no-strings micro-grant, usually monthly, to a project that adds "awesome" to their area: art, public interventions, community tech, events, science and civic...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Open call: COMPUTALA 2027 open call: Superstition and the Machine (LCB Depot x New Media Art Club, Leicester) (closes 4 Dec)
item.description:
LCB Depot with New Media Art Club
Deadline: 4 Dec 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 50 participation fee for each selected artist (funded by Arts Council England Project Grants). Free to enter. Work can be sold; the retail partner takes a 20 percent admin fee on sales.

COMPUTALA is LCB Depot's annual January season on technology in contemporary art practice, made this year with New Media Art Club.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Open call: UKRI-Funded PhD in Safe Artificial Intelligence (SAINTS Centre for Doctoral Training, University of York) 2027 (closes 11 Jan 2027)
item.description:
University of York, UKRI Centre for Doctoral Training in Safe AI (SAINTS)
Deadline: 11 Jan 2027, 12:00 GMT
Award: UK home-fee students: GBP 30,000 per year tax-free (TechFirst pilot) plus fees; international students: standard UKRI rate (GBP 21,805) plus fees. No application fee.

Fully funded doctoral studentships in the safety assurance of AI, an interdisciplinary centre where law, philosophy and sociology graduates are in scope alongside computer science, with regulators among the partners. Requires a first, or a 2:1 plus a master's. Apply by 11 January 2027, 12 noon GMT.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Jane Street Graduate Research Fellowship 2027 (tuition plus USD 50,000 stipend) (closes 13 Nov)
item.description:
Jane Street
Deadline: 13 Nov 2026
Award: Full tuition and fees for the award year plus a USD 50,000 stipend (or local-currency equivalent; taxable). Finalists receive USD 5,000. No application fee.

Jane Street's Graduate Research Fellowship supports exceptional doctoral students in electrical engineering and computer science, mathematics, physics or statistics; research does not need to relate to trading.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Digital Democracy Edinburgh 2027: Call for Proposals (TICTeC, mySociety, AI4CI, Scottish Government) (closes 15 Nov)
item.description:
mySociety (TICTeC) with the AI for Collective Intelligence (AI4CI) Hub, the Scottish Government and the Edinburgh Futures Institute, University of Edinburgh
Deadline: 15 Nov 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: NO GUARANTEED CASH, listed as an exception at the editor's request: accepted speakers get complimentary conference registration, and a limited number of travel scholarships are available for speakers who could otherwise not attend (priority to applicants from ODA-eligible countries and under-29s; amount not published). Free to submit.

Digital Democracy Edinburgh is a two-day conference from mySociety's TICTeC (The Impacts of Civic Technology) series, run with the AI for Collective Intelligence (AI4CI) Research Hub, the Scottish Government and the Edinburgh Futures Institute, for researchers, policy makers and practitioners...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Connected Canvas: The National Gallery Digital Commission 2027 (emerging UK creatives) (closes 17 Nov)
item.description:
National Gallery (National Gallery X), London
Deadline: 17 Nov 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 15,000 commission. Up to 10 shortlisted applicants receive GBP 500 each to develop proposals.

National Gallery X commissions a new digital, generative, screen-based or sound work for its three-screen LED canvas in the gallery. Open to UK-based emerging creatives in their first five years of practice who are not in full-time education.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Cryptic Nights 2027/28 Open Call (sound, performance and technology, Scotland) (closes 19 Nov)
item.description:
Cryptic, Glasgow
Deadline: 19 Nov 2026, 12:00 GMT
Award: GBP 800 fee for solo artists, up to GBP 2,000 for groups, plus residency days, mentoring, travel and access budgets.

Cryptic Nights supports emerging Scotland-based artists making work that combines original sound or music with performance, screen or technology, to develop an existing piece and present it in Cryptic's programme.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Radical Sabbatical 2027: six-month residencies on touch at the University of Birmingham (GBP 3,500 fee + GBP 500 production, UK-based artists) (closes 20 Nov)
item.description:
Eastside Projects with University Collections, University of Birmingham
Deadline: 20 Nov 2026
Award: GBP 3,500 artist fee plus GBP 500 production budget per artist; two artists selected.

Radical Sabbatical is a collaboration between Eastside Projects and University Collections at the University of Birmingham that gives two artists a six-month residency centred on research and development.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: GovAI Summer Fellowship 2027 (AI governance, London or Washington DC, GBP 14,000 for 3 months) (closes 22 Nov)
item.description:
Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
Deadline: 22 Nov 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 14,000 for 3 months plus travel support (UK Research and Applied Tracks, London); USD 24,500 plus travel support for the Washington DC track. No application fee.

GovAI's Summer Fellowship brings early-career researchers and practitioners into AI governance for three months of full-time work on a research or applied project under the mentorship of a GovAI researcher.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Cove Park Awarded Residencies 2027-2028 (Scotland, UK, Central and South America and diasporas) (closes 11 Dec)
item.description:
Cove Park
Deadline: 11 Dec 2026, 17:00 GMT
Award: Fully funded: GBP 775 per week fee (VAT inclusive, freelance), travel allowance (Scotland GBP 65 to 200, rest of UK up to GBP 250, Europe up to GBP 400, other international up to GBP 1,250), materials up to GBP 150 for studio-based practitioners, private accommodation and studio, visa and access support. Application Access Bursary available (request by 30 November 2026). No application fee.

Cove Park's biennial call for fully funded Awarded Residencies at its 50-acre rural residency site in Argyll, on the west coast of Scotland, programmed between May 2027 and December 2028.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: EVA London 2027: Call for Proposals (Electronic Visualisation and the Arts, 12-16 July 2027) (closes 11 Jan 2027)
item.description:
EVA London (BCS Computer Arts Society)
Deadline: 11 Jan 2027
Award: NO CASH, listed as an exception at the editor's request (conference presentation slot and publication in the proceedings). Free to submit, but at least one author of each paper and all panel and workshop presenters must pay conference registration (rates not yet published; to be set in spring 2027, with a special rate for Research Workshop presenters).

EVA London is a long-running hybrid conference on electronic visualisation and the arts, covering digital art, creative technology, computing and visual culture, held at BCS in Moorgate, London, and online.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Alpaca Festival 2027: Open Call for Pattern-Based Performances, Workshops and Talks (Sheffield, UK)
item.description: Pattern Club (Alpaca Festival) · deadline 01 Nov 2026 · Performances: artist fee plus national travel expenses. Workshops: artist fee, materials expenses and national travel expenses. Fee amounts are not yet confirmed (tight budget); additional costs may be covered on request. International travel is not covered beyond a small European train budget. Conference talks: no fee or expenses, in-person speakers get a free festival weekend pass and lunch on 6 and 7 May. No application fee.

item.title: Pivotal Research Fellowship (2027 Q1)
item.description: Pivotal Research · deadline 01 Nov 2026 · £15,000 to £18,000 stipend (£18,000 for senior fellows, e.g. PhD, industry track record or strong publications) + travel to and from London + £1,800/month housing for non-London fellows + weekday lunch and dinner + compute.

item.title: BRAID Creative Commissions 2027: A Promise in Return (Responsible AI, GBP 8,000-12,000, Edinburgh Art Festival)
item.description: BRAID (Bridging Responsible AI Divides), University of Edinburgh, with Inspace, the Institute for Design Informatics and the Edinburgh Futures Institute · deadline 02 Nov 2026 · Around seven commissions with budgets of GBP 8,000 to 12,000 each, inclusive of VAT and all costs. No application fee.

item.title: Institute for Law & AI: Winter Research Fellowship EU Law 2027 (Cambridge, UK)
item.description: Institute for Law & AI (LawAI) · deadline 12 Oct 2026 · GBP 1,000 weekly stipend for the 10-week fellowship (GBP 10,000 total), plus a GBP 7,000 relocation and housing payment. No application fee.
